QASHANI:92:13-17/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:92:13-17/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:92:13-17/r3.claim: The blazing fire is the great fire spanning all levels of existence through veiling, divine wrath, and punishment by effects.
QASHANI:92:13-17/r3.anchor: نارا عظيمة يبلغ لظاها جميع مراتب الوجود

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r6.claim: Verses 11–14 admonish Quraysh that God guides through revelation but does not force acceptance; they alone benefit from accepting, while both worlds remain under His control.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r6.anchor: this world and the next are in the grasp of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.claim: The warning addresses Quraysh: persistent deniers of truth face the blazing fire, while those who spend to attain purity are protected from it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.anchor: people who spend their wealth to attain purity will be shielded from this fire.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r11.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r11.claim: The majority read تلظى with one tāʾ; al-Bazzī has a doubled tāʾ, and several readers have two tāʾs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير وزيد بن علي وطلحة وسفيان بن عيينة وعبيد بن عمير: تتلظى بتاءين،

FARRA:v3p272/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p272/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p272/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ saw ʿAbd Allāh's codex spelling tatalaẓẓā with two tāʾs.
FARRA:v3p272/r1.anchor: قال الفراء ورأيتها في مصحف عبد الله: «تتلظى» بتاءين.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r6.claim: The warning to Mecca is of a flaming fire; only the wretched, who denied the Messenger and turned from faith, enters it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r6.anchor: {فأنذرتكم} يا أهل مكة، {نارا تلظى لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى} أي: تتلظى، يعني تتوقد وتتوهج

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r1.claim: The fire blazes intensely without effort from its keepers; the omitted tāʾ and assimilation suggest even the least fire of the afterlife is severe.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r1.anchor: وفي الإدغام أيضا إشارة إلى أن أدنى نار الآخرة كذلك

NAHHAS:v5p243/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p243/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p243/r2.claim: The original future form is tatalaẓẓā; a report from Ibn ʿUyayna has the unassimilated two tāʾs, while some transmitters assimilate them. Tanwīn should be vowelled before the next consonant.
NAHHAS:v5p243/r2.anchor: الأصل تتلظى وروى ابن عيينة عن عمرو

NAHHAS:v5p243/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p243/r3.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v5p243/r3.claim: He glosses talazzā as blazing intensely.

DURR-FULL:v8p536/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r6.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r6.claim: He read the warning as فأنذرتكم نارا تتلظى, with two ت letters.
DURR-FULL:v8p536/r6.anchor: وأخرج سعيد بن منصور والفراء والبيهقي في سننه بسند صحيح عن عبيد بن عمير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r1.claim: أنذرتكم may be understood as present despite past morphology, bringing the past close to the present like the conventional call that prayer has begun; this follows from God's undertaking to guide.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الفاء للتفريع المعنوي فيكون فعل ( أنذرتكم ) مرادا به الحال وإنما صيغ في صيغة المضي لتقريب زمان الماضي من الحال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r2.claim: The indefinite نارا magnifies the threat; تلظى describes fierce blazing and derives from a verb meaning to flare, with one of the original two ت letters omitted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r2.anchor: وتنكير { نارا } للتهويل ، وجملة { تلظى } نعت . وتلظى : تلتهب من شدة الاشتعال .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r10.claim: The warning may be God's direct address or a command for Muhammad to convey.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r10.anchor: وقوله تعالى: فأنذرتكم إما مخاطبة منه وإما على معنى قل لهم يا محمد،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r11.speaker: جمهور السبعة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r11.claim: Most of the seven readers pronounce talazza with an ungeminated ta.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r12.speaker: البزي عن ابن كثير وعبيد بن عمير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r12.claim: Al-Bazzi from Ibn Kathir and Ubayd ibn Umayr read the assimilated, doubled form; Ibn al-Zubayr and Talha also read two ta letters.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ البزي عن ابن كثير بشد التاء وإدغام الراء فيها

RAZI-FULL:v31p184#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#2/r1.claim: لظى means a fire that blazes, flares, and burns intensely; Hell is named لظى from this quality.

TAB-FULL:v24p478/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p478/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p478/r1.claim: The warning concerns the blazing Fire of Hell; people should avoid disobeying or disbelieving in God lest they enter it. The form تلظى is treated as a future verb with the extra tāʾ omitted.
TAB-FULL:v24p478/r1.anchor: صلي النار التي تلظى التقي، ووضع أفعل موضع فعيل

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura develops two antitheses: behavior and recompense for the saved and damned, first in verses 5–13 and then in verses 14–21.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.anchor: Es folgen zwei Antithesen (V. 5–13 und V. 14–21), welche die Verhaltensweisen und Jenseitsschicksale von Seligen und Verdammten miteinander kontrastieren

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.claim: The final stanza reverses the earlier order of saved and damned; the outer blessed sections are linked by ittaqā in verse 5 and ʾatqā in verse 17.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.anchor: Zum einen wird die Reihenfolge Seliger – Verdammter (V. 5–7 und V. 8–11) jetzt invertiert (V. 14–16 Verdammter, V. 17–20 Seliger)

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.claim: The stanza halves mirror one another: earlier behavior lists precede reward or warning, while the final warning and promise precede each group's worldly conduct.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.anchor: In V. 5–7 und V. 8–11 ging zunächst ein Tugend- bzw. Lasterkatalog voraus, auf den dann jeweils ein Drohwort bzw. eine Verheißung folgten

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r3.claim: The second antithesis concretizes the first: verse 14 resolves the enigmatic threat of verse 10 as the image of blazing Hell.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r4.claim: This movement from riddle to shocking disclosure resembles the teaching question and explicit Hell image in 104:4–7 and the eschatological resolution in 102:3–8.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r4.anchor: Eine analoge Sequenz aus Enigma und eschatologischer Auflösung liegt Q 102:3–8 zu Grunde

TABRISI:92:14-21/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:14-21/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:92:14-21/r1.claim: The threatened Fire blazes, flares, and burns intensely.
TABRISI:92:14-21/r1.anchor: أي خوفتكم نارا تتلهب وتتوهج وتتوقد

THALABI:v10p218#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p218#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p218#2/r1.claim: The threatened fire blazes and flares up.

THALABI:v10p218#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p218#2/r2.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
THALABI:v10p218#2/r2.claim: He reads the word with a second tāʾ, preserving its original form; other readers omit it.
THALABI:v10p218#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ عبيد بن عمير (تتلظى) على الأصل، وغيره على الحذف

THALABI:v10p218#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p218#2/r4.speaker: مالك عن عمر بن عبد العزيز
THALABI:v10p218#2/r4.claim: While reciting the threat of the blazing fire in prayer, Umar began to weep and could not continue the verse, so he read another sura.
THALABI:v10p218#2/r4.anchor: حدثنا مالك قال: صلى بنا عمر بن عبد العزيز المغرب

ELMALILI:92:12-21/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r4.claim: The warning announces a Fire that blazes and grows increasingly fierce.
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r4.anchor: bir ateş haber verdim ki alevlendikçe alevlenir, köpürdükçe köpürür.

ELMALILI:92:12-21/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r5.claim: Talazzā is a feminine imperfect verb whose original form is tatalaẓẓā; as a past verb with feminine nār, it would be talazzat.
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r5.anchor: “Telezzâ (تَلَظَّىٰ)” muzâri‘müennes, aslı “tetelezzâ”dır (تتلظى). Mazi olsa idi -nâr müennes olduğu için- تلظت denilmesi lâzım gelirdi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.claim: Others say verses 5–19 were revealed about Abu Bakr; regardless of a specific occasion, the message and rulings are general.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.anchor: bazıları ise 5-19. âyetlerin (bk. Elmalılı, VIII, 5881), müşriklerin işkence ettiği köleleri satın alıp âzat ederek hürriyetlerine kavuşturan Hz. Ebû Bekir hakkında indiğini söylemişlerdir. Âyetler böyle bir özel olay üzerine gelmiş olsa da, hükümleri ve mesajları geneldir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.claim: After warning of the blazing fire in verse 14, verses 17–20 describe giving for God's sake without owing anyone, spiritual purification, and being kept from the fire.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.anchor: 14. âyette muhataplar “alev alev yanan ateş”e karşı uyarıldıktan sonra 17-20. âyetlerde, birine borçlu olmadıkları, kimsenin kendilerinde bir hakkı bulunmadığı halde bile

IBNASHUR:92:14/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:14/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:14/r1.claim: If “I warned you” is past tense in its literal sense, fa introduces a detailed warning from the previous general warning, much like an explanatory fa.
IBNASHUR:92:14/r1.anchor: يجوز أن تكون الفاء لمجرد التفريع الذِكري

IBNASHUR:92:14/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:14/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:14/r2.claim: Alternatively, the past form can describe a present warning, drawing past time close to the present; then the warning follows from God's undertaking to guide.
IBNASHUR:92:14/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الفاء للتفريع المعنوي فيكون فعلُ

IBNASHUR:92:14/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:14/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:14/r3.claim: The indefinite noun “fire” magnifies its terror, and telazzā describes its intense blazing.

IBNASHUR:92:14/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:14/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:14/r4.claim: The verb comes from laẓiyat al-nār, “the fire blazed”; its original form tatalaẓẓā lost one of the two tāʾs for brevity.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r5.claim: The fā may simply continue the discourse if the earlier warning is literal past speech; it introduces a detailed warning branching from the preceding general warning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r5.anchor: يجوز أن تكون الفاء لمجرد التفريع الذكري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#3/r1.claim: The Fire blazes and flares up.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#3/r1.anchor: فأنذرتكم نارا تلظى أي توقد وتتوهج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r4.claim: Mujahid says the blazing fire is flaring and burning brightly.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r5.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r5.claim: The Prophet repeatedly warns that he is warning people of the Fire, loudly enough that a person in the market could hear; his cloak slips from his shoulder to his feet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r5.anchor: عن سماك بن حرب، سمعت النعمان بن بشير يخطب يقول: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يخطب يقول: "أنذركم النار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r6.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r6.claim: The Prophet says the least punished person in Hell will have two embers beneath his feet that make his brain boil; al-Bukhari also transmits the report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r6.anchor: حدثني أبو إسحاق: سمعت النعمان ابن بشير يخطب ويقول: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "إن أهون أهل النار عذابا يوم القيامة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r7.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r7.claim: A Muslim version describes the least-punished person wearing sandals and straps of fire so his brain boils like a cauldron, while he thinks no one suffers more than him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r7.anchor: عن الأعمش، عن أبي إسحاق، عن النعمان بن بشير قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن أهون أهل النار عذابا من له نعلان وشراكان من نار

FARRA:v3p271/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p271/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p271/r7.claim: Talazzā is an imperfect verb, “it blazes”; if it were a past-tense verb the form would be talazzat.
FARRA:v3p271/r7.anchor: معناه: تتلظى فهي في موضع رفع، ولو كانت على معنى فعل ماض لكانت: فأنذرتكم نارا تلظت.

JISHUMI:v10p7444/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r6.speaker: ابن كثير
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr geminates the tā in تلظى; others lighten it. The gemination is explained as assimilation or as assimilation of tanwīn.
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r6.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير: تلظى بتشديد التاء، الباقون بالتخفيف

JISHUMI:v10p7444/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r7.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r7.claim: He reads تتلظى with two tāʾs, preserving the original form; other readers have one by deletion.
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r7.anchor: وقرأ عبيد بن عمير: (تتلظى) بتاءين على الأصل، غيره بتاء واحدة

JISHUMI:v10p7444/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r9.claim: Talazzī means a fire blazing intensely; laẓā is a name for Hell derived from the same root.
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r9.anchor: والتلظي: تلهب النار بشدة الإيقاد، وتلظى وتوهج وتلهب نظائر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r1.speaker: أبو الزبير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r1.claim: Abu al-Zubayr reads the verb with an extra ta: tatalaẓẓā.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p769/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p769/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p769/r1.claim: A report promises that one who recites al-Layl will receive until contentment, be spared hardship, and find ease made easy.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p769/r1.anchor: وعن رسول صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1309 ) ( من قرأ سورة والليل

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r7.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r7.claim: He interprets talazzā as seething with anger.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r8.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r8.claim: He interprets talazzā as catching fire.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r9.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r9.claim: He interprets talazzā as glowing intensely; Ali's poem illustrates the word.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r9.anchor: تتوهج , قاله مجاهد , وأنشد لعلي رضي الله عنه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r10.speaker: علي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r10.claim: His verse compares a glowing fire to salt mixed into something and shining like agate in shade.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r10.anchor: كأن الملح خالطه إذا ما … تلظى كالعقيقة في الظلال

MUJAHID:v2p765#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p765#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p765#3/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the blazing fire as one that flares or burns intensely.
MUJAHID:v2p765#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ نارا تلظى ﴾ يقول توهج

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#15/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#15/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#15/r1.claim: The warning means “I frightened you” of a Fire that blazes fiercely.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r1.claim: Anzartukum means “I warned and frightened you.”
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فأنذرتكم } أي حذرتكم وخوفتكم

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r2.claim: Talazza means blazing; the underlying form is tatallaza.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r2.anchor: { نارا تلظى } أي تلهب وتتوقد. وأصله تتلظى

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r3.speaker: عبيد بن عمير، يحيى بن يعمر، طلحة بن مصرف
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r3.claim: They read the full form tatallaza.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r3.anchor: وهي قراءة عبيد بن عمير، ويحيى بن يعمر، وطلحة بن مصرف

QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r8.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r8.claim: Malik says Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz wept while reciting the warning and had to leave it for another sura.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:14-16/r8.anchor: وقال مالك: صلى بنا عمر بن عبد العزيز المغرب، فقرأ

QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.claim: An alternative contextual account identifies the giver as Abu al-Dahdah and the miser as the Ansari palm owner; it maps ease to Paradise, hardship to Hell, and death to loss of wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.anchor: { فأما من أعطى واتقى } يعني أبا الدحداح. { وصدق بالحسنى } أي بالثواب

QUTB-ZILAL:92:14/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:14/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:14/r1.claim: Because God clarified guidance and owns both abodes of action and recompense, He warns people of the blazing fire.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:14/r1.anchor: تفريعا على أن الله كتب على نفسه بيان الهدى للعباد ، وأن له الآخرة والأولى داري الجزاء والعمل

RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r1.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r1.claim: Al-Qaffal says the sura was revealed about Abu Bakr's spending on Muslims and Umayya ibn Khalaf's miserliness and disbelief, while its message applies generally.
RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r1.anchor: قال القفال رحمه الله : نزلت هذه السورة في أبي بكر

RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r2.claim: Its general scope is evident from statements that human striving differs and that the audience is warned of a blazing Fire.
RAZI-FULL:v31p179/r2.anchor: إلا أنها وإن كانت كذلك لكن معانيها عامة للناس

RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r4.claim: The Qadi's claim that the warning names only a particular blazing fire is weak, since the phrase can describe all Hell; another verse calls it a blaze that strips the skin.
RAZI-FULL:v31p184#3/r4.anchor: لأن قوله : { نارا تلظى } يحتمل أن يكون ذلك صفة لكل النيران

SAMIN-DURR:92:14/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:14/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:92:14/r1.claim: Al-Bazzī doubles the tāʾ of talazzā; the meeting of two quiescent letters is awkward, like the cited form in 24:15.
SAMIN-DURR:92:14/r1.anchor: أن البزي يشدد مثل التاء، والتشديد فيها عسر لالتقاء الساكنين فيها على غير حدهما

SAMIN-DURR:92:14/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:14/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:92:14/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ describes a reading with kasra on tanwīn and doubled tāʾ; the author calls it rare but regular because it avoids the forbidden meeting of two quiescent letters.
SAMIN-DURR:92:14/r2.anchor: يقرأ بكسر التنوين وتشديد التاء، وقد ذكر وجهه عند

SAMIN-DURR:92:14/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:14/r3.speaker: ابن الزبير، سفيان، زيد بن علي، طلحة
SAMIN-DURR:92:14/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr, Sufyān, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and Ṭalḥa read tatalaẓẓā with two tāʾs, the original form.
SAMIN-DURR:92:14/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير وسفيان وزيد بن علي وطلحة " تتلظى " بتاءين وهو الأصل

STUDYQURAN:92:14/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:14/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:14/r1.claim: Hell is elsewhere described as a crushing Fire.
STUDYQURAN:92:14/r1.anchor: Elsewhere Hell is described as a crushing Fire

TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r1.claim: The warning is about blazing Hell and urges people to avoid disobedience and disbelief so they will not enter it.
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {نارا تلظى} [الليل: 14] قال: توهج

TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r2.claim: Tilazzā is a present-tense verb with an elided initial tāʾ; if it were past tense it would be talazzat.
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r2.anchor: فعلا ماضيا لقيل: فأنذرتكم نارا تلظت وبنحو الذي قلنا في ذلك قال أهل التأويل

TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r3.claim: Mujāhid glosses the fire's description as blazing.
TAB-FULL:v24p476#3/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {نارا تلظى} [الليل: 14] قال: توهج

TABATABAI:92:13-16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r4.claim: The warning of blazing fire follows from God’s guidance; the shift to “I warned you” marks God as the ultimate warner, though the message is delivered through His messenger.
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r4.anchor: وبذلك يوجه ما في قوله { فأنذرتكم } من الالتفات عن التكلم مع الغير إلى التكلم وحده

TABATABAI:92:13-16/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r5.claim: Talazzī means the fire’s flaring and blazing; the fire is Hell, called laẓā elsewhere.
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r5.anchor: وتلظى النار تلهبها وتوهجها، والمراد بالنار التي تتلظى جهنم

THALABI:v10p220/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r1.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v10p220/r1.claim: A man refused the Prophet’s offer of a date palm in Paradise for his palm that dropped fruit into a neighbor’s yard; Abū al-Daḥdāḥ bought and donated it, and the Prophet transferred it to the neighbor. The account identifies them with the surah’s contrasting figures.
THALABI:v10p220/r1.anchor: عطاء قال: كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة، وكان له جار، فكان يسقط من بلحها في دار جاره

THALABI:v10p220/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p220/r3.claim: The palm’s owner represents the miser who deems himself self-sufficient and denies reward; he is eased toward Hell and is the “most wretched” who enters the blazing fire.
THALABI:v10p220/r3.anchor: وأما من بخل واستغنى يعني الأنصاري وكذب بالحسنى يعني الثواب فسنيسره للعسرى يعني النار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86/r1.claim: The people being warned are the people of Mecca.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86/r2.claim: Talaẓẓā describes a fire flaring, glowing, and blazing; the verb is talaẓẓat, and Hell is called Laẓā from the same root.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p86/r2.anchor: {فأنذرتكم نارا تلظى} تتوقد وتتوهج وتتلهب، يقال: تلظت النار تتلظى تلظيا.

WAHIDI-QT:92:14/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:14/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:14/r1.claim: The warning made the audience afraid of a fire that blazes.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14:anmerkung/r1.claim: The warning fire is compared with 70:15, and the note on nār is at 111:3.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Vgl. 70:15 (kallā ʾinnahā laẓā). Zu nār vgl. die Anmerkung zu 111:3.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14:anmerkung/r2.claim: This is probably the earliest Quranic attestation of ʾanḏara and the n-dh-r root; more early-Makkan examples are listed at 74:36.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Der Vers ist der wohl früheste koranische Beleg für das Verb ʾanḏara und allgemein für die Wurzel n-ḏ-r

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:14/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:14/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:14/r1.claim: Alongside showing people the right path, God warns through revelation and prophets against Hell, the consequence of following the wrong path.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:14/r1.anchor: yanlış yolda gitmenin sonucu olan cehenneme karşı da onları vahiy ve peygamberleri aracılığıyla uyarmıştır

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p381/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p381/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p381/r3.claim: Al-Layl mentions warning without glad tidings, so it names the Fire alone; Paradise would be a promise of good outside this warning passage’s purpose.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p381/r3.anchor: ذكر الله تعالى الإنذار ولم يذكر التبشير ولذلك اقتصر على ذكر النار

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p382/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p382/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p382/r1.claim: The past tense frames a single, completed warning of one thing, the blazing Fire; warnings tied to ongoing revelation use the present tense.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p382/r1.anchor: جاء الفعل بصيغة المضارع لأن الله تعالى أنذرهم هنا بشيء واحد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p382/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p382/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p382/r2.claim: Al-Naba’s warning is emphatic because its warning is extended and repeated throughout the sūra; al-Layl gives one warning in one verse and needs no added emphasis.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p382/r2.anchor: سورة النبأ فيها توكيد لأن الإنذار في سورة النبأ

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p421/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p421/r1.speaker: البزي عن ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p421/r1.claim: Al-Bazzī from Ibn Kathīr geminates the tāʾ in تلظى; Qunbul through al-Nabbāl and the other readers lighten it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p421/r1.anchor: البزي عن ابن كثير: نارا تلظى [14] مشددة التاء، قنبل عن النبال يخفف وكذلك الباقون

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p421/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p421/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p421/r2.claim: Gemination is harder here than in تلقف because a consonant precedes the tāʾ and the assimilated tāʾ is itself silent, not a glide.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p421/r2.anchor: وذلك أن قبل التاء ساكنا، والتاء المدغمة ساكنة، وليس حرف لين.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p421/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p421/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p421/r3.claim: The pattern could be compared with disjunct لا تناجوا or, if the silent خاء of تخطف can assimilate, with that reading; تلقف was not assimilated here for the stated phonetic reason.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p421/r3.anchor: ومن قال: تخطف* فأسكن الخاء مع إدغام تاء تفتعل في الطاء، جاز على قوله: نارا تلظى،

QIRAAT-ER:92:14:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:92:14:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:92:14:4#1/r1.claim: Assimilating the Form V prefix tāʾ creates a geminate tt, a phonetic intensification matching the semantic intensity.
QIRAAT-ER:92:14:4#1/r1.anchor: Assimilation of the tāʾ: the original Form V tāʾ prefix assimilates

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#3/r1.claim: The warning branches from God's undertaking to guide: He guided by warning them; تلظى means blaze and is contracted from تتلظى by dropping one of the two initial tāʾs.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#3/r1.anchor: قيل متفرع على كون الهدى عليه سبحانه أي فهديتكم بالإنذار وبالغت في هدايتكم وتلظي بمعنى تلتهب وأصله تتلظى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#3/r2.speaker: ابن الزبير
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#3/r2.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Ṭalḥa, Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna, and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read the form with both tāʾs.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#3/r2.anchor: وقد قرأ بذلك ابن الزبير وزيد بن علي وطلحة وسفيان بن عيينة وعبيد بن عمير

BINTSHATI:v2p112/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p112/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p112/r6.claim: In this warning, لظى means a pure flame and تلظى means the fire blazes; elsewhere لظى is a name for Hell.
BINTSHATI:v2p112/r6.anchor: واللظى في العربية اللهب الخالص، والتلظى تسعر النار واحتدام توقدها

NASHR:v2p233/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p233/r2.speaker: الجعبري
NASHR:v2p233/r2.claim: Al-Jaʿbarī allows either retaining sukūn or kasra in ten cases where two sukūns meet, including these examples; the poem says the majority retained sukūn while some readers used kasra.
NASHR:v2p233/r2.anchor: كلام الجعبري في شرحه فقال: وفيها وجهان - يعني في العشرة التي اجتمع فيها الساكنان - صحيحان نحو هل تربصون

NASHR:v2p233/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p233/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p233/r3.claim: Although al-Jaʿbarī reported kasra in نارا تلظى, the author finds no earlier precedent or transmission from the reading authorities; recitation is inherited by transmission, not inferred from grammatical permission.
NASHR:v2p233/r3.anchor: ولو جاز الكسر لجاز الابتداء بهمزة وصل، وهذا وإن جاز عند أهل العربية في الكلام فإنه غير جائز عند القراء

ABUHAYYAN:92:14/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:14/r1.speaker: ابن الزبير وزيد بن علي وطلحة وسفيان بن عيينة وعبيد بن عمير والبزي والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:92:14/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Ṭalḥah, Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read tatalaẓẓā with two tāʾs; al-Bazzī doubles tāʾ, while the majority read one tāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN:92:14/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير وزيد بن علي وطلحة وسفيان بن عيينة وعبيد بن عمير : تتلظى بتاءين

ALUSI:92:14/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:14/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:14/r1.claim: The warning follows from the preceding statement that guidance rests with God: He guides by warning the audience and intensifies that guidance.
ALUSI:92:14/r1.anchor: قيل متفرع على كون الهدى عليه سبحانه أي فهديتكم بالإنذار وبالغت في هدايتكم

ALUSI:92:14/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:14/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:14/r2.claim: Talazzā means to blaze; its original form is tatalaẓẓā with two tāʾs, one of which is deleted.
ALUSI:92:14/r2.anchor: وتلظى بمعنى تلتهب وأصله تتلظى بتاءين فحذفت منه إحداهما

ALUSI:92:14/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:14/r3.speaker: ابن الزبير وزيد بن علي وطلحة وسفيان بن عيينة وعبيد بن عمير
ALUSI:92:14/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Ṭalḥa, Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read the fuller form with both tāʾs.
ALUSI:92:14/r3.anchor: وقد قرأ بذلك ابن الزبير وزيد بن علي وطلحة وسفيان بن عيينة وعبيد بن عمير

BAGHAWI:92:14/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:14/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:92:14/r1.claim: The warning is addressed to the people of Mecca.
BAGHAWI:92:14/r1.anchor: { فأنذرتكم } يا أهل مكة ، { ناراً تلظى }

BAGHAWI:92:14/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:14/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:92:14/r2.claim: Telazzā means it blazes and glows; it is an expanded form of tat alazzā.
BAGHAWI:92:14/r2.anchor: { ناراً تلظى } يعني : تتلظى ، يعني تتوقد وتتوهج

BAYDAWI:92:14/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:14/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:14/r1.claim: Talazzā means to blaze or flare up.
BAYDAWI:92:14/r1.anchor: {فأنذرتكم نارا تلظى} (14) فأنذرتكم نارا تلظى تتلهب

BIQAI:92:14/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:14/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:14/r1.claim: After establishing God's dominion, knowledge, and power, the discourse turns to warning; the first-person singular softens the address, bringing understanding near and distancing apprehension.
BIQAI:92:14/r1.anchor: شرح ذلك بما سبب عنه من قوله لافتاً القول إلى تجريد الضمير من مظهر العظمة للترقق بالمخاطبين

BIQAI:92:14/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:14/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:14/r2.claim: The fire blazes with extreme intensity, without effort for its kindler or keepers; dropping the tāʾ and assimilating the sounds suggest even the least fire of the hereafter is so, making the warning a fortiori.
BIQAI:92:14/r2.anchor: بما أشار إليه إسقاط التاء ،   وفي الإدغام أيضاً إشارة إلى أن أدنى نار الآخرة كذلك

DURR:92:14/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:14/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR:92:14/r1.claim: Qatada says God clarifies the lawful and unlawful, obedience and disobedience, and glosses the blazing fire as glowing.
DURR:92:14/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { إن علينا للهدى } يقول : على الله البيان بيان حلاله وحرامه

DURR:92:14/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:14/r2.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
DURR:92:14/r2.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr recited “tatalazzā” with two tāʾs; al-Suyuti states that the chain is sound.
DURR:92:14/r2.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير أنه قرأ : «فأنذرتكم ناراً تتلظى

IBNATIYYA:92:14/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:14/r1.speaker: جمهور السبعة
IBNATIYYA:92:14/r1.claim: Most of the Seven read talazzā with a light tāʾ.

IBNATIYYA:92:14/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:14/r2.speaker: البزي
IBNATIYYA:92:14/r2.claim: Al-Bazzī, transmitting from Ibn Kathīr, geminates the tāʾ and assimilates the rāʾ into it; ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr also reads it this way.
IBNATIYYA:92:14/r2.anchor: وقرأ البزي عن ابن كثير بشد التاء وإدغام الراء فيها . وقرأها كذلك عبيد بن عمير

IBNATIYYA:92:14/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:14/r3.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
IBNATIYYA:92:14/r3.claim: Another reading attributed to ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr has two tāʾs, as do Ibn al-Zubayr and Ṭalḥa.
IBNATIYYA:92:14/r3.anchor: وروي أيضاً عنه «تتلظى » بتاءين وكذلك قرأ ابن الزبير وطلحة

IBNKATHIR:92:14/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:14/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR:92:14/r1.claim: Mujāhid glosses the fire described as blazing as kindled and aflame.
IBNKATHIR:92:14/r1.anchor: وقوله : { فَأَنْذَرْتُكُمْ نَارًا تَلَظَّى } قال مجاهد : أي توهج .

IBNKATHIR:92:14/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:14/r2.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
IBNKATHIR:92:14/r2.claim: Al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr heard the Prophet repeatedly warn of the Fire; the warning could be heard in the market, and his cloak fell from his shoulder to his feet.
IBNKATHIR:92:14/r2.anchor: سمعتُ النعمان بن بشير يخطب يقول : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يخطب يقول

IBNKATHIR:92:14/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:14/r3.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
IBNKATHIR:92:14/r3.claim: The Prophet said the least punished person in Hell will have two live coals under his feet that boil his brain; Ibn Kathīr cites al-Bukhārī.
IBNKATHIR:92:14/r3.anchor: حدثني أبو إسحاق : سمعت النعمان ابن بشير يخطب ويقول : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

IBNKATHIR:92:14/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:14/r4.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
IBNKATHIR:92:14/r4.claim: Muslim's version says the least punished wears two fiery sandals and straps that boil his brain like a pot; he imagines no one suffers more, though he suffers least.
IBNKATHIR:92:14/r4.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق ، عن النعمان بن بشير قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF:92:14/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:14/r1.speaker: أبو الزبير
KASHSHAF:92:14/r1.claim: Abū al-Zubayr reads the word with an added tāʾ: “tatalazzā.”

MAWARDI:92:14/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:14/r1.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI:92:14/r1.claim: Talazzā means that the Fire fumes with anger.

MAWARDI:92:14/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:14/r2.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI:92:14/r2.claim: Talazzā means that the Fire blazes.

MAWARDI:92:14/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:14/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI:92:14/r3.claim: Talazzā means that the Fire glows; a line attributed to ʿAlī illustrates the word.
MAWARDI:92:14/r3.anchor: الثالث : تتوهج ، قاله مجاهد ، وأنشد لعلي رضي الله عنه

NASAFI:92:14/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:14/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:14/r1.claim: “I warned you” means I frightened you.

NASAFI:92:14/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:14/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:14/r2.claim: The fire “talazzā” means a fire that blazes.

QURTUBI:92:14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:14/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:14/r1.claim: The address means: I warned you and made you fear the punishment.

QURTUBI:92:14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:14/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:14/r2.claim: The fire blazes and burns; the form is originally tatalaẓẓā.

QURTUBI:92:14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:14/r3.speaker: عبيد بن عمير ويحيى بن يعمر وطلحة بن مصرف
QURTUBI:92:14/r3.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, and Ṭalḥah ibn Muṣarrif read the fuller form تتلظى.
QURTUBI:92:14/r3.anchor: وهي قراءة عبيد بن عمير ، ويحيى بن يعمر ، وطلحة بن مصرف

RAZI:92:14/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:14/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:92:14/r1.claim: Talazzā means to catch fire, blaze, and glow; the verb is used of a fire blazing, and Jahannam is called Laẓā from it.

TAB:92:14/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:14/r1.speaker: author
TAB:92:14/r1.claim: The warning is of blazing Hell: people should avoid disobeying and denying God in this life lest they burn in it in the afterlife.
TAB:92:14/r1.anchor: فأنذرتكم أيها الناس نارا تتوهّج ،   وهي نار جهنم ،   يقول :  احذروا أن تعصوا ربكم في الدنيا

TAB:92:14/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:14/r2.speaker: author
TAB:92:14/r2.claim: Talazzā is the present verb tatalazzā, grammatically nominative; a past form would be talazzat.
TAB:92:14/r2.anchor: تلظّى ،   وإنما هي تتلظّى ،   وهي في موضع رفع ،   لأنه فعل مستقبل ،   ولو كان فعلاً ماضيا لقيل :  فأنذرتكم نارا تلظّت .

TAB:92:14/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:14/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:92:14/r3.claim: Mujāhid glosses the fire's description as blazing or flaring.
TAB:92:14/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   في قول الله :  نارا تَلَظّى قال :  تَوَهّج .

ITQAN:v3p162/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p162/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p162/r1.claim: When either element could be omitted, the second is usually omitted; examples include forms in which the second predicate or genitive is understood.
ITQAN:v3p162/r1.anchor: إذا دار الأمر بين كون المحذوف أولا أو ثانيا فكونه ثانيا أولى

NASHR:v2p231/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p231/r5.speaker: البزي
NASHR:v2p231/r5.claim: The section lists 31 future verbs whose initial tāʾ may double, across the cited passages; al-Bazzi transmits doubling in the stated routes, including the forms at 20:69 and 49:13.
NASHR:v2p231/r5.anchor: وذلك في إحدى وثلاثين تاء، وهي ولا تيمموا الخبيث هنا،

DURR:92:12/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:12/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR:92:12/r2.claim: Qatada glosses the neighboring phrase “blazing fire” as a blaze or flare.
DURR:92:12/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { إن علينا للهدى } يقول : على الله البيان

IBNATIYYA:92:13/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:13/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:13/r2.claim: The following phrase fa-andhartukum can be direct address, or an implied command to Muhammad to tell them.
IBNATIYYA:92:13/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { فأنذرتكم } إما مخاطبة وإما على معنى قل لهم يا محمد

RAZI:92:15/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r7.speaker: القاضي
RAZI:92:15/r7.claim: Al-Qāḍī first proposes that “blazing fire” is a particular tier of Hell, so the verse does not rule out sinners entering other tiers.
RAZI:92:15/r7.anchor: أن يكون المراد بقوله : { نارا تلظى } نارا مخصوصة من النيران ، لأنها دركات

RAZI:92:15/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r8.speaker: القاضي
RAZI:92:15/r8.claim: Al-Qāḍī alternatively takes “blazing fire” as all Hell, but reads the restriction as saying the most wretched alone is most entitled to it.
RAZI:92:15/r8.anchor: ( الثاني ) : أن المراد بقوله : { نارا تلظى } النيران أجمع ، ويكون المراد بقوله : { لا يصلاها إلا الأشقى } أي هذا الأشقى به أحق

RAZI:92:15/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:15/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:92:15/r12.claim: Al-Razi rejects a specific tier: the phrase can describe every fire or one fire, but another verse calls all Hell laẓā.
RAZI:92:15/r12.anchor: لأن قوله : { نارا تلظى } يحتمل أن يكون ذلك صفة لكل النيران ، وأن يكون صفة لنار مخصوصة

RAZI:92:16/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:16/r7.speaker: القاضي
RAZI:92:16/r7.claim: Al-Qāḍī first proposes that “blazing fire” is a particular tier of Hell, so the verse does not rule out sinners entering other tiers.
RAZI:92:16/r7.anchor: أن يكون المراد بقوله : { نارا تلظى } نارا مخصوصة من النيران ، لأنها دركات

RAZI:92:16/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:16/r8.speaker: القاضي

RAZI:92:16/r12.speaker: author

RAZI:92:16/r12.anchor: لأن قوله : { نارا تلظى } يحتمل أن يكون ذلك صفة لكل النيران ، وأن يكون صفة لنار مخصوصة
